PGP 2025-27 | Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad

EDUCATION
PGP, IIM Ahmedabad, 2025-27, CGPA 3.0/4.33

- Head, Hostel Mess Committee, IIT Bombay (2019-20): managed a budget of INR 1.2 crore

EXTRACURRICULAR
- Completed the Ladakh Marathon (2023)

interview.resume_text:
Ishaan Kulkarni
PGP 2025-27 | Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad

EDUCATION
PGP, IIM Ahmedabad, 2025-27, CGPA 3.0/4.33
B.Tech, Chemical Engineering, IIT Bombay, 2021, 8.0/10

WORK EXPERIENCE (36 months)
Asian Paints, Ankleshwar plant | Production Engineer | Jul 2021 - Jun 2024
- Ran the emulsion section on rotating shifts with 35 operators; raised batch yield from 92.1% to 95.4%
- Led a Kaizen team that cut changeover time on the tinting line from 70 to 40 minutes
- Coordinated with the union committee during a 3-day contract-worker stoppage in 2023

SUMMER INTERNSHIP
Aditya Birla Group, Group Executive Office | Strategy Intern | Apr - Jun 2026
- Evaluated 3 adjacencies for the group's chemicals business; recommended specialty adhesives, now under deeper study
- Built the business case for a 50 KTPA plant; IRR of 19% under base-case assumptions

POSITIONS OF RESPONSIBILITY
- Secretary, Rural Immersion Program, IIM Ahmedabad: placed 80 students with 14 NGOs in Gujarat
- Head, Hostel Mess Committee, IIT Bombay (2019-20): managed a budget of INR 1.2 crore

EXTRACURRICULAR
- Completed the Ladakh Marathon (2023)

topics.question: Let’s move to a broader business judgment question. How would you decide whether a proposed adjacency deserves investment when the market looks attractive but the company lacks capabilities?
answer_plan: Assess market attractiveness through demand, growth, customer need, competition, and the company’s right to win.
Compare the missing capabilities with the economics and time required to build, partner, or acquire them.
Test the business case under different assumptions, including investment, margins, execution risk, and likely returns.
Make a recommendation that explains the trade-off and identifies a small validation step before full investment.
topics.example_answer: I would first test whether the market is attractive through demand, growth, customer needs, competition, and expected margins. Then I would compare the capabilities required with what the company already has and estimate the cost and time to build, partner, or acquire the gaps. I would stress-test the business case under different assumptions and assess execution risk. I would invest only if the company has a credible right to win and the expected returns justify the capability gap; otherwise, I would recommend a partnership or a limited pilot first.
